subject: biology
title: Command words and how to answer

scenes.heading: Command words and how to answer
scenes.sub: The one word that decides your marks
scenes.say: You can know everything about a topic and still lose marks. Why? Because you didn't do what the question asked. Every question starts with a command word. Let's learn to read it.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A canteen order: say exactly what you want
scenes.science: A command word is the examiner's order for your answer
scenes.breaks: A canteen worker might guess what you meant. An assessor only marks what you actually write.
scenes.say: Think of a canteen order. Say food, please, and you won't get what you wanted. The command word is the examiner's order. Identify is just the sausage roll. Explain is the full order plus why. But a canteen worker might guess what you meant. An assessor only marks what's on the page.

scenes.heading: Describe vs explain
scenes.say: This is where most marks are lost. Describe is the what: like a commentator saying what happened. Explain is the why or how: like a coach linking cause and effect. If your answer has no because or therefore, it's probably just a description.

scenes.heading: More command words
points: Identify: give a fact or term, no reasons
scenes.say: Identify means give a fact or a term. Compare needs similarities and differences: use both, and whereas. Analyse means trend, data with units, then interpretation. Evaluate weighs strengths and limitations, then gives a verdict, like a judge. And justify means claim, because, evidence.

scenes.heading: Plan every answer
steps: Count marks: one idea per mark
Answer in context with key terms
scenes.say: Use this routine. Circle the command word. Underline the content and context. Count the marks and plan roughly one correct idea per mark. Answer in the context of the question, using biology terms. Then re-read the question to check.

scenes.heading: Explain (3 marks)
scenes.question: Explain why oxygen can cross the plasma membrane by simple diffusion but glucose cannot.
lines: …so it passes through the hydrophobic core
Glucose is larger and polar, so it's repelled
So glucose needs protein channels or carriers
scenes.say: Try this three mark explain question. A weak answer says oxygen is small and glucose is big. A strong answer links each property to the membrane. Oxygen is small and non-polar, so it passes through the hydrophobic core. Glucose is larger and polar, so it's repelled. Therefore glucose needs protein channels or carriers.

Quick recap. Read the command word before anything else. Describe tells what, explain tells why. Analyse means trend, data and interpretation. And plan one correct idea per mark, in the context of the question. Now try the practice questions!
